meta.title: Past Perfect Continuous Tenses
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Past Perfect Continuous Tenses themed around work and office environments.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Past Perfect Continuous tense paired with topics like passive voice, relative clauses, gerunds, inversion, conditionals, and more, all within familiar workplace contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the CEO arrived, the staff _____ for the board meeting for over two hours.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with a time clause. 'Had been preparing' emphasizes the duration of an ongoing action that was completed right before another past action ('arrived').
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous for actions in progress up to a specific past moment
explanation.formula: By the time + past simple, subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: By the time the boss called, we had been working on the report for hours.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with stative verbs. Verbs expressing mental states like 'know' are generally not used in continuous tenses; the Past Perfect ('had known') must be used instead.
explanation.concept: Avoiding continuous forms for stative verbs in past narratives
explanation.formula: Subject + had + past participle (stative verb)
examples: She had understood the policy before the meeting started.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: The software developers, who _____ all night to fix the critical bug, were completely exhausted by morning.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with non-defining relative clauses. 'Had been coding' describes an ongoing action in the past that continued up to another past moment ('were exhausted').
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous in relative clauses to describe duration before a past event
explanation.formula: Noun, who + had been + verb-ing, + past simple verb
examples: The team, which had been negotiating for weeks, finally signed the deal.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. The verb 'avoid' must be followed by a gerund ('taking'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Verbs requiring gerund complements in past narratives
explanation.formula: Subject + avoided + verb-ing
examples: He avoided answering the difficult questions during the interview.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: Before the merger was officially announced, the executives _____ in secret for several months.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with conjunctions of time. 'Had been negotiating' emphasizes the duration of the action leading up to the past event ('was announced').
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous with 'before' to show duration prior to a past event
explanation.formula: Before + past simple, subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: Before the project launched, they had been testing it for months.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with quantifiers. 'Feedback' is an uncountable noun, so it must be preceded by 'little of', not 'few of' (which is used for countable nouns).
explanation.concept: Correct quantifier usage with uncountable nouns in past narratives
explanation.formula: Little of + uncountable noun + past simple verb
examples: Little of the advice was useful.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: Rarely _____ so harmoniously before that major project was completed.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Rarely' at the beginning of a sentence triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('had the team been working').
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative adverbs in Past Perfect Continuous
explanation.formula: Rarely + had + subject + been + verb-ing
examples: Never had the department been performing so well.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with preposition collocations. The verb 'rely' is always followed by the preposition 'on', not 'in'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific verbs in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + had been + relying on + noun
examples: We had been relying on the old database for years.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the mixed conditional sentence.
data.question: If she _____ overtime last month, she wouldn't be so exhausted at work right now.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with mixed conditionals. The 'if' clause refers to an ongoing past action ('hadn't been working'), while the main clause refers to a present result ('wouldn't be').
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous in the 'if' clause of a mixed conditional
explanation.formula: If + subject + hadn't been + verb-ing, subject + would + base verb
examples: If I hadn't been driving so fast, I wouldn't be so stressed now.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with subject-verb agreement rules. 'The number of' takes a singular verb, while 'a number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb ('were').
explanation.concept: Agreement with 'the number of' vs. 'a number of'
explanation.formula: The number of + singular verb; a number of + plural noun + plural verb
examples: The number of errors has dropped, but a number of issues remain.

data.hint: Choose the correct discourse marker to complete the sentence.
data.question: The department had been underfunded for years; _____, they had been achieving remarkable results.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with contrastive discourse markers. 'Nevertheless' is required to show the contrast between being underfunded and achieving remarkable results.
explanation.concept: Using contrastive discourse markers with past perfect continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Past perfect continuous clause; nevertheless, + past perfect continuous clause
examples: They had been struggling with budget cuts; nevertheless, they had been delivering quality work.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. The phrasal verb 'look forward to' uses 'to' as a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund ('meeting'), not a base verb.
explanation.concept: Using gerunds after prepositional phrasal verbs in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + had been + looking forward to + verb-ing
examples: I had been looking forward to seeing the new office layout.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the cleft sentence.
data.question: It was the marketing team that _____ the campaign's success before the rebrand.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with cleft sentences for emphasis. 'Had been driving' highlights the duration of the action leading up to a specific past point ('the rebrand').
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous in it-cleft structures
explanation.formula: It + was + noun + that + had been + verb-ing
examples: It was the IT department that had been resolving the issues all night.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with adverb placement. Adverbs of frequency like 'constantly' must be placed between the auxiliary 'had' and 'been', or after 'been', but standard placement is 'had been constantly reviewing' or 'had constantly been reviewing'. 'Had been constantly' is the most natural fit here.
explanation.concept: Correct positioning of frequency adverbs in past perfect continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + had been + adverb + verb-ing
examples: He had been constantly checking his emails.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: The servers crashed because they _____ continuously for weeks without proper maintenance.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with cause-and-effect conjunctions. 'Had been running' explains the ongoing past action that led to the past result ('crashed').
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous to show the cause of a past event
explanation.formula: Past simple result + because + subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: The pipe burst because it had been freezing all night.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with ellipsis. In parallel structures, 'too' is less formal than 'as well' when ellipsing the continuous verb phrase, but more importantly, 'had been as well' correctly parallels the continuous aspect without the awkward 'had been too'.
explanation.concept: Omitting repeated verbs in parallel past perfect continuous structures
explanation.formula: Subject + had been + verb-ing, and + subject + had been + as well
examples: The managers had been planning the event, and the staff had been as well.

data.hint: Choose the correct comparative structure to complete the sentence.
data.question: The longer the contract negotiations _____, the more frustrated the stakeholders became.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with advanced comparative structures. 'Had been dragging on' emphasizes the accumulating duration of the action leading up to the past result.
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous in double comparative structures
explanation.formula: The longer + subject + had been + verb-ing, the more + adjective + subject + past simple
examples: The harder he had been working, the more tired he became.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before words starting with a /j/ sound
explanation.formula: Subject + had been + verb-ing + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: He had been using a unique strategy.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the noun clause.
data.question: What surprised the board was that the compliance committee _____ the warning signs for months.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with noun clauses. 'Had been ignoring' indicates an ongoing action in the past that continued up to the moment of surprise.
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous in noun clauses following past tense verbs
explanation.formula: What + past simple + was that + subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: What shocked me was that they had been lying all along.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with relative pronouns. The relative pronoun referring to a person ('employees') must be 'who' (or 'that'), not 'which' (which is used for things).
explanation.concept: Choosing the correct relative pronoun for people in continuous relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun (people) + who + had been + verb-ing
examples: The staff who had been waiting were finally called in.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: Not only _____ its sales quotas, but the department had also been mentoring new hires.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with 'not only... but also' inversion. 'Not only' at the beginning of a clause triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('had the department been exceeding').
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'not only' in past perfect continuous structures
explanation.formula: Not only + had + subject + been + verb-ing, but + subject + had + also + been + verb-ing
examples: Not only had she been leading the project, but she had also been training the team.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with the 'it's high time' structure. 'It's high time' requires the past subjunctive ('recognized'). Additionally, 'department' is a singular collective noun, requiring 'has been'.
explanation.topic: Past Perfect Continuous + It's High Time
explanation.concept: Past subjunctive and singular agreement in 'it's high time' structures
explanation.formula: It is high time + subject + past simple + that + singular subject + has been + verb-ing
examples: It is high time we acknowledged that the team has been working overtime.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: He acted as though he _____ the company for decades, even though he was just a new intern.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with 'as though' unreal comparisons. 'Had been managing' describes an unreal, ongoing past situation that contradicts the reality ('was just a new intern').
explanation.topic: Past Perfect Continuous + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous for unreal comparisons about the past
explanation.formula: Subject + past simple + as though + subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: She spoke as though she had been working there for years.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective/adverb' inversion with the Past Perfect Continuous. The result clause should use the Simple Past ('had resigned') to show the completed action resulting from the prolonged waiting, not the continuous form.
explanation.topic: Past Perfect Continuous + So / Such Inversion
explanation.concept: Using Simple Past for the result of a 'so... that' inversion with Past Perfect Continuous
explanation.formula: So + adverb + had + subject + been + verb-ing + that + subject + past simple
examples: So long had they been waiting that they gave up.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: Under no circumstances _____ about the financial discrepancies before the official audit was published.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous passive tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Under no circumstances' at the beginning triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('had the auditors been informed').
explanation.topic: Past Perfect Continuous + Negative Adverbial Inversion
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative phrases in Past Perfect Continuous passive
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + had + subject + been + past participle
examples: Under no circumstances had the data been compromised.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with conditional inversion. 'Had' must be followed by 'been' + present participle ('failing') to form the Past Perfect Continuous, not the base verb 'fail'.
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect after inverted conditional 'had'
explanation.formula: Had + subject + been + verb-ing, subject + would have + past participle
examples: Had the system been failing, we would have noticed.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: Little did the new hire know that the department _____ a major restructuring for months.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with negative adverbial inversion ('Little did... know'). 'Had been undergoing' emphasizes the ongoing duration of the restructuring up to the moment the new hire found out.
explanation.topic: Past Perfect Continuous + Little Did He Know
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous in noun clauses following inverted past simple verbs
explanation.formula: Little + did + subject + know + that + subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: Little did I know that they had been planning a surprise.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with perfect participle clauses. The perfect passive/continuous participle requires 'Having been' + present participle ('working') to show an action completed before the main past action.
explanation.concept: Using perfect continuous participles to show duration before a past event
explanation.formula: Having been + verb-ing, subject + past simple verb
examples: Having been working all day, he was exhausted.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: I wish I _____ more attention during the compliance training sessions last month.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense with 'wish' for past regret. 'Had been paying' expresses regret about an ongoing action (or lack thereof) in the past.
explanation.topic: Past Perfect Continuous + Wish / If Only
explanation.concept: Using Past Perfect Continuous to express regret about past ongoing actions
explanation.formula: I wish + subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: I wish I had been listening more carefully.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with 'future in the past'. When describing a future perfect continuous action from the perspective of the past ('knew'), 'will' must be backshifted to 'would'.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Future in the Past
explanation.concept: Backshifting 'will' to 'would' in future perfect continuous contexts reported from the past
explanation.formula: Subject + past simple + that + subject + would have been + verb-ing
examples: He knew that he would have been working there for a decade by then.
